answer.rationale:
The timeline is the strongest signal available: the release landed 2h ago and write-path p99 began climbing 90 minutes ago, so the release is the leading suspect and removing the suspected cause is preferable to masking it. Regional failover (memory_b2) and added capacity (memory_b3) address infrastructure-side degradation and would carry a bad build with them; circuit breakers (memory_b4) protect against an external dependency failure, which is not what is indicated here; read-replica routing (memory_b5) helps read/dashboard pressure on the primary, and this is a write-path problem, so it is at best partial relief. That said, memory_b5 is not fully excluded, because settlement peak plus report load could be compounding the primary, so I am holding that as the live alternative if the rollback hypothesis fails.

I want memory_b1 verified because it is the single memory my intended action rests on, and its most load-bearing clause is the weakest: 'the rollback finished without customer impact.' The archived record should tell me whether that rollback ran at comparable write volume and whether the prior build's schema/state was compatible. A clean rollback at low traffic on day 18 is very weak evidence that a rollback is clean during peak settlement writes, and it is also possible the day-18 incident was an error spike rather than a latency ramp, which would make it a different failure mode than what I am facing.

Downstream risk: this is a payments write path at daily peak, so an aborted or migration-incompatible rollback could drop or duplicate in-flight settlement writes, which directly violates 'without losing customer writes' and is far worse than the current elevated latency. I am therefore scoping this as a small guarded rollback, draining and rolling back one cohort behind staged gating (per memory_b6, whose canary machinery already exists here) with write-integrity checks and reconciliation counts before any wider fan-out. If the cohort's p99 does not recover, the release is exonerated, I stop, and I spend the next window on read-replica routing instead of widening a rollback that is not working. I am also aware that consuming the single intervention slot means the alternative waits, so the guarded scope is chosen partly to keep the diagnostic value high per unit of risk.
